title: Section-normalized constant-module small-site transport
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$ and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, with $R=\mathcal O_E$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. For a scheme $T$, use the original small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] and its exact small-model module equivalence $C_T=\mathrm{sfCbcModelModules}(T,R)$ from [lem-sf-constant-semilinear-generator-comparison]. For $f:V\to T$ there is a unique natural isomorphism $f_*C_T\cong C_Vf_*^{\rm model}$ whose underlying-section map, followed by the canonical constantDirectUnderlying comparison, is the identity on every section. Define ordinaryDirectModel to be this uniquely section-normalized isomorphism. Define towerModel to apply $C_T$ termwise to strict $\mathbf N^{\rm op}$-towers and derivedTowerModel to be its exact derived functor. These retain the original site object universe and morphism universe.

source.place: Step 5: canonical small-site coordinates and proper/open construction required to state the explicit integral comparison obligation.

proof.text: Whisker constantDirectUnderlying with sfCbcModelModules V. Its target underlying-set functor is definitionally the underlying sheaf of sfCbcModelModules T after the original module direct image. Naturality of the inverse comparison, applied to biproduct inclusions and projections, proves additivity on each section.
Apply the local scalar compatibility lemma to the inverse underlying comparison. Together with additivity and naturality this defines a natural transformation of module sheaves.

The two inverse identities of the underlying comparison prove bijectivity on every section. ModuleCat reflects bijectivity as invertibility; the functor from module sheaves to module presheaves reflects isomorphisms. Thus the natural transformation is an isomorphism and its hom satisfies exactly the displayed section normalization.

For any other normalized isomorphism, apply the inverse of constantDirectUnderlying to its normalization equation. The inverse identities force equality of every section map; extensionality for module sheaf maps, natural transformations and isomorphisms gives uniqueness. Choose this unique isomorphism as before. The tower and derived tower transports and their exactness instances are unchanged.
